raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

FLUX.3 modulates every token separately, so its blocks pass per-token shift/scale tensors to `fused_norm_scale_shift`. The fused CUDA kernel (`kda_kernels/norm_scale_shift`) only handled one shift/scale row per batch, so on Blackwell every FLUX.3 block fell back to the slower CuTe-DSL kernel. This PR adds a per-token variant of the fused kernel and routes those calls to it.

## Modifications

- `norm_scale_shift.cuh`: a `kPerTokenMod` template parameter that offsets the shift/scale loads by the token row, and a `NormScaleShiftPerTokenKernel` BF16 entry point (non-residual path).
- `norm_scale_shift_jit.py`: `try_fused_norm_scale_shift` keeps the per-batch row path and additionally dispatches contiguous per-token shift/scale (`[1, S, D]` or `[S, D]`, matching `x`) to the new entry point. Other inputs still fall back to CuTe-DSL as before.
- `test_norm.py`:
  - The per-token path matches the CuTe-DSL reference for FLUX.3 token counts (text stream and 1024x1024 joint stream) and both modulation ranks, and the public `fused_norm_scale_shift` op returns the same output.
  - Strided (non-contiguous) per-token modulation is rejected and falls back.

## Accuracy Tests

Kernel-level: the per-token kernel matches the CuTe-DSL reference (`test_norm.py`, atol/rtol 5e-2). Against an FP32 reference on B200, both kernels have the same max abs error (~0.03) at every token count in the table below.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Kernel, B200, per-token shift/scale, hidden 3072, cold L2 (`marker.do_bench`):

| Tokens | Fused (this PR) | CuTe-DSL fallback | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1,024 | 5.2 us | 6.5 us | 1.25x |
| 4,608 | 17.7 us | 22.0 us | 1.24x |
| 9,216 | 33.9 us | 41.6 us | 1.23x |
| 18,432 | 65.3 us | 80.9 us | 1.24x |

At 9k tokens the fused kernel reaches ~84% of B200 HBM bandwidth (CuTe-DSL: ~68%).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not needed: no new flags or user-facing behavior.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

@@ -73,6 +73,18 @@ def _row_bf16(t, device: torch.device):
     return row if _aligned(row) else None
 
 
+def _per_token_bf16(t, x):
+    """``t`` as an ``[N, D]`` view when it holds one row per token of ``x``."""
+    if (
+        not isinstance(t, torch.Tensor)
+        or t.shape not in (x.shape, x.shape[1:])
+        or not t.is_contiguous()
+        or not _nss_activation(t.view(x.shape), x)
+    ):
+        return None
+    return t.view(-1, _HIDDEN)
+
+
 @cache_once
 def norm_scale_shift_module() -> Module:
     device = torch.device("cuda", torch.cuda.current_device())
@@ -88,6 +100,10 @@ def norm_scale_shift_module() -> Module:
                 "nss_bf16_row",
                 "norm_scale_shift::NormScaleShiftKernel::run",
             ),
+            (
+                "nss_bf16_token",
+                "norm_scale_shift::NormScaleShiftPerTokenKernel::run",
+            ),
             (
                 "srnss_bf16_row",
                 "norm_scale_shift::ScaleResidualNormScaleShiftKernel::run",
@@ -178,14 +194,21 @@ def try_fused_norm_scale_shift(x, weight, bias, scale, shift, norm_type, eps):
     if not _nss_activation(x) or not _blackwell_or_newer(x.device):
         return None
 
-    scale = _row_bf16(scale, x.device)
-    shift = _row_bf16(shift, x.device)
-    if scale is None or shift is None:
-        return None
-
     y = torch.empty_like(x)
-    _module().nss_bf16_row(
-        y.view(-1, _HIDDEN), x.view(-1, _HIDDEN), scale, shift, float(eps)
+    row_scale = _row_bf16(scale, x.device)
+    row_shift = _row_bf16(shift, x.device)
+    if row_scale is not None and row_shift is not None:
+        _module().nss_bf16_row(
+            y.view(-1, _HIDDEN), x.view(-1, _HIDDEN), row_scale, row_shift, float(eps)
+        )
+        return y
+
+    token_scale = _per_token_bf16(scale, x)
+    token_shift = _per_token_bf16(shift, x)
+    if token_scale is None or token_shift is None:
+        return None
+    _module().nss_bf16_token(
+        y.view(-1, _HIDDEN), x.view(-1, _HIDDEN), token_scale, token_shift, float(eps)
     )
     return y

@@ -508,6 +508,45 @@ def test_cutedsl_scale_residual_gate_index_modes(norm_type, index_mode):
     _run_cute(True, norm_type=norm_type, gate_mode=index_mode)
 
 
+def _native_norm_scale_shift():
+    fused_norm_scale_shift, _ = _import_cutedsl()
+    if torch.cuda.get_device_capability()[0] < 10:
+        pytest.skip("native norm-scale-shift requires SM100+")
+    from sglang.kernels.kda_kernels import norm_scale_shift_jit
+
+    return fused_norm_scale_shift, norm_scale_shift_jit.try_fused_norm_scale_shift
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tokens", [160, 8352])  # FLUX.3 text / 1024^2 joint stream
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("mod_rank", [2, 3])
+@torch.no_grad()
+def test_native_norm_scale_shift_per_token_modulation(tokens, mod_rank):
+    fused_norm_scale_shift, try_native = _native_norm_scale_shift()
+    x = torch.randn(1, tokens, 3072, device=DEVICE, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    mod_shape = x.shape if mod_rank == 3 else x.shape[1:]
+    scale = 0.1 * torch.randn(mod_shape, device=DEVICE, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    shift = 0.1 * torch.randn(mod_shape, device=DEVICE, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+
+    y = try_native(x, None, None, scale, shift, "layer", EPS)
+    assert y is not None
+    y_ref, _ = _cute_reference(
+        None, x, None, None, None, scale.view_as(x), shift.view_as(x), "layer", EPS
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(y, y_ref, atol=5e-2, rtol=5e-2)
+    assert torch.equal(
+        fused_norm_scale_shift(x, None, None, scale, shift, "layer", EPS), y
+    )
+
+
+@torch.no_grad()
+def test_native_norm_scale_shift_rejects_strided_per_token_modulation():
+    _, try_native = _native_norm_scale_shift()
+    x = torch.randn(1, 256, 3072, device=DEVICE, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    packed = torch.randn(1, 256, 2 * 3072, device=DEVICE, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    scale, shift = packed.chunk(2, dim=-1)
+    assert try_native(x, None, None, scale, shift, "layer", EPS) is None
+
+
 def test_validate_scale_shift_rejects_non_divisible_frames():
     _import_cutedsl()
